Speech chunk:
criminal records, but the record of conviction will be purged from the system. It is a fact that records of conviction and copies of records of conviction are contained all over Canada in court houses, in municipal police force offices and with the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, which maintains a registry for that purpose. The registry is called CPIC and is a record keeping system that the RCMP retains. It keeps a record of all the convictions that it manages to get its hands on across the country. It also keeps track of all the other criminal records, records of the criminal procedure, not just records of conviction. It is a fact that not all records of conviction are given to the RCMP. I see, Mr. Speaker, you might like to interrupt at this point. We can continue the debate later.
